source: Http2StreamWriteStallHandler.selectStalledStreams: stream 1 takes the whole connection window and its client returns none of it; stream 3, with its own window open, waits on the closed connection window. Stream 1 is reset at its timeout, which gives stream 3 one fresh period (a release grant) instead of resetting it in the same check; its client returns nothing, so stream 3 is reset one period later

steps.note: stream 1: a 70 kB response, the first 65535 bytes of which close both its own and the connection window; stream 3: a small response delayed so that it finds the connection window closed. The client returns no window
stream 1 reset alone: stream 3 was given a fresh period, so for a period the count stays at one (resetting both in one check would jump from 0 to 2)

mask.reason: only the series this scenario drives; the rest are pinned by metrics.json
